title: Capstone: retail lakehouse from landing to a Gold star
objective_text: Build a small lakehouse end to end: land new days through a parameterised notebook, MERGE them into Silver with quality checks, keep a type 2 customer dimension, and build a Gold fact table and a denormalised aggregate, so that a rerun changes nothing.
scenario: A shop drops each day's orders and customer changes into landing. Orders get sent twice, corrected days later, or sent for customers who don't exist yet; customer changes arrive out of order. Finance wants daily sales by customer segment as it was when each sale happened, and operations wants proof that no day lands twice.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: landing.orders and landing.customers with three days of files, bronze.products, empty bronze.orders, bronze.customers, silver.orders and ops.load_log, the notebook land_day in notebooks/, and a starter answer.py that lands one day.
required: ops.load_log has one row per day ever landed, with rows_landed, the number land_day exited with for that day.
silver.orders has one row per order: its newest load. An order whose newest row has no customer_id or a quantity that isn't positive isn't in it.
silver.orders_rejected has those orders: order_id, the load_date of their newest row, and reason 'missing customer_id' or 'quantity not positive' (the first that applies).

silver.dim_customer has a version per change of city or segment, in changed_at order; a row that changes neither adds no version. customer_key is customer_id * 100 + the version number from 1. valid_to is the next version's valid_from, NULL for the current one. name is the latest name on every version.

gold.fact_sales has a row per order in silver.orders with the customer_key of the version valid at order_ts, or -1 when there isn't one; order_date is the order_ts date and amount is qty * unit_price.
gold.sales_by_segment has orders and amount per order_date, segment (from the version on the sale, 'Unknown' for -1) and product category.

verifies: After your code runs, the six tables hold the right rows on the exercise data and on data you haven't seen, starting from a lakehouse where a day has already landed, on this PC.
No day lands twice, the dimension has a unique surrogate key, and running your code again changes nothing.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in Fabric, and land_day runs here as a notebook called from yours, not from a pipeline's Notebook activity. Pipelines are E31 and E19.
Table maintenance: OPTIMIZE, V-Order and VACUUM on the Gold tables are E56, and query tuning is E59 and E64.
How you build each table: the grading checks the tables, so a full rebuild of Silver that gives the same rows also passes.
hints: Read ops.load_log before landing anything: the days to land are the load_dates in landing that aren't in the log.
notebookutils.notebook.run returns the exit value as a string; int() it before you log it.
An order can arrive again on a later day, corrected. Rank each order's rows by load_date, newest first, and judge the order by that row.
A MERGE can delete as well as update: whenMatchedDelete with a condition removes an order whose correction made it invalid.
Build the dimension from all of bronze.customers, ordered by changed_at, so a change that arrives last still lands in its place. lag() over that order tells you whether city or segment changed.
Join each order to the version where valid_from <= order_ts and order_ts is before valid_to (or valid_to is NULL). A LEFT JOIN keeps orders whose customer hasn't arrived.
explanation: The load log is the watermark: landing a day appends to Bronze, so a day must land once, and the log says which days have. Silver takes the newest load of each order, because a later day can correct an earlier one, and the quality checks judge that newest row; a MERGE with a delete clause handles a correction that makes an order invalid, while rejected orders are kept with a reason rather than lost. The customer dimension is type 2 on city and segment: a version per real change, in the order the changes happened rather than the order they arrived, with valid_from and valid_to, while the name is type 1. The fact table joins each order to the version valid when it was placed, so a later move doesn't rewrite history, and orders for customers who haven't arrived get the Unknown key -1 instead of disappearing; because the dimension and Gold are rebuilt from history, those orders pick up the right key when the customer lands. The aggregate denormalises segment and category onto the sales. Every step can run again: nothing lands twice, and the same history gives the same tables.
troubleshooting: ops.load_log has a day twice: the code landed days that were already in the log.
Order 1002 has quantity 1: the oldest load won. Rank by load_date, newest first.
A customer who moved and moved back is missing a version: compare each change with the one before it in changed_at order, not in the order the rows arrived.
Customer 1 has two versions with the same city and segment: a row that changes neither adds no version.
Order 1011 is missing from Gold: an inner join dropped the customer that hasn't arrived. Use -1.
reset: Reset rebuilds landing, bronze, silver.orders and ops.load_log from setup.sql, removes the tables your runs made, and puts the starter back.
review_notes: LOCAL VERIFIED on DuckDB's PySpark API with delta-rs; the shop data is synthetic and the same every time.

Objectives 2.2.5 (pipelines), 3.3.1 (OPTIMIZE) and 3.3.6 (query performance) from the plan aren't claimed: this engine can't run a pipeline or OPTIMIZE, so they stay with E31, E56, E59 and E64 and the Fabric verified version.

Learn facts used (2026-11-07): notebookutils.notebook.run returns the exit value as a string; type 2 dimensions keep history with validity columns and surrogate keys; an unknown member stands in for a missing dimension row.
